newsitem.title: INDIA: NEW INDIA BOND AT 100.4 RUPEES, 12.59 PCT 2004 UP.
newsitem.headline: NEW INDIA BOND AT 100.4 RUPEES, 12.59 PCT 2004 UP.

text.p: Indian government securities were mixed in late morning deals Tuesday and dealers said market attention was focussed on two bonds.
They said the 11.19 percent 2005, auctioned on Monday and the 12.59 percent 2004 were both up but other stocks were steady or down.
The 11.19 percent 2005 bond, auctioned at par on Monday, was traded at 100.40 rupees while the 12.59 percent 2004 rose to 106.95 from Monday's 106.65.
"The 12.59 percent 2004 gives almost the same yield as the 2005 paper even though its tenure is shorter by one year," said a money market dealer.
"This is why traders are buying up the (12.59) stock. It is already quoting 107 rupees."
Among other stocks, the 11.55 percent 2002 moved up to 102.15 from 102.11 while the 10.85 percent 2001 slipped to 100.69 from 100.70.
Dealers said high call money rates will keep trade on a low key on Tuesday in most stocks other than the 12.59 percent 2004 and the 11.19 percent 2005.
Call money was traded around 7.75-8.25 percent in late morning, up from Monday's close of 4.5-5.0 percent on funds outflows from banks.
The Reserve Bank of India on Monday auctioned 30 billion rupees of eight year bonds and payments by successful bidders is due today.
